name: Ziad Ahmed
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Redefy at 14 in 2013 and JUV Consulting at 17 in 2016, growing JUV to work with 30+ Fortune 500 companies and being named to Forbes 30 Under 30 at 19.
starting_point: Born to a Muslim-Bangladeshi American family in New Jersey; raised in a supportive household that encouraged civic engagement from a young age.
current_position: Head of Next Gen at United Talent Agency (UTA) after UTA acquired JUV Consulting in 2024; based in NYC.

trajectory.title: Founded Redefy
trajectory.description: Founded Redefy, a youth-led nonprofit committed to defying stereotypes and fostering inclusivity, while in middle school.

trajectory.title: Founded JUV Consulting
trajectory.description: Launched JUV Consulting, a Gen Z marketing consultancy, while still in high school, connecting brands with young audiences.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in Marketing & Advertising at age 19 for his work building JUV Consulting into the largest Gen Z agency.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Yale University
trajectory.description: Graduated from Yale University, where he focused his research on social media's impact on policy-making.

trajectory.title: Selected as Obama USA Leader
trajectory.description: Named an inaugural United States Obama Leader by the Obama Foundation for his work championing young voices.

trajectory.title: UTA acquired JUV Consulting
trajectory.description: United Talent Agency acquired JUV Consulting, forming UTA Marketing's Next Gen Practice with Ziad as Head of Next Gen.

name: Jahkil Jackson
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Project I Am at age 8 in 2016, growing it to distribute over 300,000 Blessing Bags and raise nearly $1M for people experiencing homelessness worldwide.
starting_point: Born in Chicago, Illinois; inspired by his aunt who took him to feed the homeless at age 5, and supported by his parents and grandmother in launching his initiative.
current_position: Founder of Project I Am, 3-time bestselling author, TEDx speaker, and CNN Hero Young Wonder; continuing to expand Project I Am globally from Chicago.

trajectory.title: Founded Project I Am
trajectory.description: Launched Project I Am at age 8 with his parents' help, distributing Blessing Bags filled with essentials to people experiencing homelessness in Chicago.

trajectory.title: Recognized by Obama Foundation
trajectory.description: Featured by the Obama Foundation as one of the world's most influential young changemakers, gaining national media attention.

trajectory.title: Named CNN Hero Young Wonder
trajectory.description: Honored as a CNN Hero Young Wonder and Marvel Hero for his philanthropic work distributing Blessing Bags.

trajectory.title: Published first book
trajectory.description: Published his first bestselling book, sharing his journey as a youth social entrepreneur and inspiring other young people.

trajectory.title: Expanded internationally
trajectory.description: Project I Am expanded internationally, distributing Blessing Bags in Ghana, Eswatini, India, London, and disaster-stricken areas.

trajectory.title: Published second book
trajectory.description: Published 'Don't Wait To Be Great,' his second bestselling book about combining community service and entrepreneurship.

trajectory.title: Celebrated 10-year anniversary
trajectory.description: Project I Am celebrated its 10-year anniversary, having raised nearly $1M and impacted over 300,000 people worldwide.

name: Xiuhtezcatl Martinez
milestone_by_age_26: Served as Youth Director of Earth Guardians, addressed the UN General Assembly at 15, and was a lead plaintiff in the landmark Juliana v. United States climate lawsuit filed at 15.
starting_point: Born in Colorado to a family deeply rooted in environmental activism; his mother co-founded Earth Guardians and his father raised him in the Aztec/Mexica indigenous tradition emphasizing stewardship of nature.
current_position: Environmental activist and hip-hop artist based in Portland, Oregon; continues to perform and advocate for climate justice.

trajectory.title: First climate activism speech
trajectory.description: Delivered his first public appeal to a Colorado city council at age 9, asking them to ban pesticides in city parks.

trajectory.title: Filed Martinez v. Colorado Oil and Gas
trajectory.description: Became one of seven plaintiffs in a state-level climate lawsuit against the Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation Commission at age 13.

trajectory.title: Addressed UN General Assembly
trajectory.description: Delivered a speech at the United Nations General Assembly in English, Spanish, and Nahuatl, gaining international recognition.

trajectory.title: Lead plaintiff in Juliana v. United States
trajectory.description: Became one of 21 plaintiffs in the landmark Juliana v. United States climate lawsuit against the U.S. government.

trajectory.title: Published 'We Rise' book
trajectory.description: Published his book 'We Rise: The Earth Guardians Guide to Building a Movement That Restores the Planet.'

trajectory.title: Stepped down as Youth Director of Earth Guardians
trajectory.description: Transitioned from his role as Youth Director of Earth Guardians, continuing activism through music and performance.

name: Delaney Reynolds
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Sink or Swim Project at age 15, led the first solar mandate in Florida, and served as lead plaintiff in Reynolds v. State of Florida climate lawsuit.
starting_point: Born and raised in Miami, Florida, with family roots in the Florida Keys spanning four generations; grew up between Miami and a solar-powered community on No Name Key.
current_position: Graduate student pursuing a dual J.D. and Ph.D. at the University of Miami's Abess Center for Ecosystem Science and Policy; Founder & CEO of the Sink or Swim Project.

trajectory.title: Founded the Sink or Swim Project
trajectory.description: Founded the Sink or Swim Project at age 15, an educational and political advocacy organization focused on climate change and sea level rise in South Florida.

trajectory.title: Led first solar mandate in Florida
trajectory.description: Wrote and implemented the first solar mandate in Florida in the City of South Miami, a groundbreaking local clean energy policy.

trajectory.title: Lead plaintiff in Reynolds v. State of Florida
trajectory.description: Served as lead plaintiff in the Reynolds v. State of Florida climate change lawsuit, arguing the state had a constitutional duty to protect the climate.

trajectory.title: Addressed UN General Assembly
trajectory.description: Addressed the General Assembly of the United Nations in New York City on climate change and sea level rise.

trajectory.title: Co-authored Florida renewable energy rule
trajectory.description: Petitioned, co-authored, and implemented the first piece of climate legislation in Florida in over two decades, setting a goal of 100% renewable energy by 2050.

trajectory.title: Joined Lighthiser v. Trump lawsuit
trajectory.description: Became a plaintiff in the Lighthiser v. Trump federal climate case, continuing her 11-year advocacy career for climate protection.

name: Mari Copeny
milestone_by_age_26: Wrote a letter to President Obama at age 8 in 2016 that prompted his visit to Flint and $100M in federal funding, and raised over $500K for clean water through the Little Miss Flint Clean Water Fund.
starting_point: Born July 6, 2007 in Flint, Michigan; grew up in a Black, low-income community directly affected by the Flint water crisis that began in 2014.
current_position: 18-year-old activist, philanthropist, and clean water advocate based in Flint, Michigan; continues distributing school supplies, toys, and water filters through her various initiatives.

trajectory.title: Wrote letter to President Obama
trajectory.description: Wrote a letter to President Obama at age 8 about the Flint water crisis, prompting his visit to Flint and $100M in federal funding to address the crisis.

trajectory.title: Spoke at Stand Up to Trump rally
trajectory.description: Addressed a large crowd at the 'Stand Up to Trump' rally in front of the White House, demanding the president fulfill his campaign promise to fix Flint's water.

trajectory.title: Raised over $100,000 for water initiatives
trajectory.description: Raised over $100,000 for water filters and clean water initiatives through partnerships and crowdfunding campaigns.

trajectory.title: Partnered with Hydroviv for water filters
trajectory.description: Partnered with Hydroviv to create her own water filter brand, with proceeds funding filter donations to families in need.

trajectory.title: Named Time's 25 Most Influential Teens
trajectory.description: Named one of Time magazine's 25 Most Influential Teens for her ongoing clean water advocacy.

trajectory.title: Received Billboard Music Award Changemaker
trajectory.description: Received the Changemaker Award at the Billboard Music Awards at age 14 for her commitment to individual action and leadership.

trajectory.title: 10-year anniversary of water crisis advocacy
trajectory.description: Stood at City Hall on the 10-year anniversary of the Flint water crisis, continuing to demand clean water for residents.

name: Jon Jones
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest UFC champion in history at age 23 by defeating Shogun Rua for the UFC Light Heavyweight Championship at UFC 128 on March 19, 2011.
starting_point: Born July 19, 1987 in Rochester, New York; raised in a family of athletes with brothers Arthur (NFL player) and Chandler (NFL player); father was a pastor.
current_position: Retired from MMA in 2025; former UFC Heavyweight Champion, widely regarded as one of the greatest mixed martial artists of all time.

trajectory.title: Professional MMA debut
trajectory.description: Made his professional MMA debut, quickly building an undefeated record with his unorthodox fighting style learned partly from YouTube videos.

trajectory.title: Youngest UFC champion in history
trajectory.description: Defeated Mauricio 'Shogun' Rua at UFC 128 on March 19, 2011 to become the youngest champion in UFC history at age 23.

trajectory.title: Broke title defense record
trajectory.description: Broke Tito Ortiz's record for most UFC light heavyweight title defenses with eight successful defenses, including wins over Rashad Evans and Chael Sonnen.

trajectory.title: Stripped of title after arrest
trajectory.description: Stripped of the light heavyweight title and removed from UFC rankings after being arrested on felony hit-and-run charges.

trajectory.title: Reclaimed light heavyweight title
trajectory.description: Returned to reclaim the UFC light heavyweight championship by defeating Alexander Gustafsson at UFC 232.

trajectory.title: Vacated light heavyweight title
trajectory.description: Voluntarily vacated the UFC light heavyweight title in August 2020 to pursue a move to the heavyweight division.

trajectory.title: Won UFC heavyweight title
trajectory.description: Submitted Ciryl Gane at UFC 285 to win the vacant UFC heavyweight title, becoming a two-division champion.

trajectory.title: Defended heavyweight title against Miocic
trajectory.description: Stopped Stipe Miocic via TKO at UFC 309 to retain the UFC heavyweight title in a dominant performance.

trajectory.title: Retired from MMA
trajectory.description: Vacated the UFC heavyweight title and retired from professional mixed martial arts in June 2025.

name: Ronda Rousey
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Strikeforce Women's Bantamweight Championship at age 25 in March 2012, then became the inaugural UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion later that year.
starting_point: Born February 1, 1987 in Riverside, California; mother AnnMaria De Mars was a world judo champion; father committed suicide when she was 8; born with umbilical cord complications causing mild brain damage and childhood apraxia of speech.
current_position: Former UFC champion and WWE wrestler; returned to MMA in 2026 for a fight against Gina Carano; also an actress and author.

trajectory.title: Youngest Olympic judo qualifier
trajectory.description: Became the youngest judoka to qualify for the 2004 Olympics in Athens at age 17.

trajectory.title: Olympic bronze medal in judo
trajectory.description: Won bronze at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming the first American woman to win an Olympic medal in judo.

trajectory.title: Amateur MMA debut
trajectory.description: Made her amateur MMA debut in August 2010, winning by armbar in 23 seconds, followed by three more amateur wins all by first-round armbar.

trajectory.title: Professional MMA debut
trajectory.description: Turned professional in March 2011, winning her debut by armbar in under a minute at a King of the Cage event.

trajectory.title: Strikeforce and UFC champion
trajectory.description: Won the Strikeforce Women's Bantamweight Championship by defeating Miesha Tate in March, then became the inaugural UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion in November.

trajectory.title: First UFC women's title defense
trajectory.description: Headlined UFC 157, the first women's fight in UFC history, defeating Liz Carmouche by armbar in the first UFC women's title defense.

trajectory.title: First career loss to Holly Holm
trajectory.description: Suffered her first MMA loss at UFC 193, knocked out by Holly Holm with a head kick, ending her dominant championship reign.

trajectory.title: Retired from MMA
trajectory.description: Lost to Amanda Nunes at UFC 207 in 48 seconds and retired from MMA competition.

trajectory.title: Inducted into UFC Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Became the first female fighter inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame.

trajectory.title: WWE debut and championship
trajectory.description: Debuted in WWE and won the Raw Women's Championship, becoming one of only eight female Triple Crown champions in WWE history.

name: Max Holloway
milestone_by_age_26: Won the interim UFC Featherweight Championship at age 25 by defeating Anthony Pettis at UFC 206 on December 10, 2016, then unified the title by beating Jose Aldo at UFC 212 on June 3, 2017.
starting_point: Born December 4, 1991 in Honolulu, Hawaii; raised in Wai'anae, an area known for fighting; of Native Hawaiian and Samoan descent; father left when he was 11, mother struggled with drug addiction before recovering.
current_position: Competing in the UFC lightweight division; former UFC Featherweight Champion and BMF titleholder; ranked among the greatest featherweights of all time.

trajectory.title: Am MMA debut
trajectory.description: Amassed a 4-0 amateur record and turned professional, gaining recognition as a top featherweight prospect.

trajectory.title: UFC debut as youngest fighter on roster
trajectory.description: Made his UFC debut at age 20 against Dustin Poirier at UFC 143, becoming the youngest fighter on the UFC roster at the time.

trajectory.title: Won interim UFC featherweight title
trajectory.description: Defeated Anthony Pettis at UFC 206 on December 10, 2016 to win the interim UFC Featherweight Championship.

trajectory.title: Unified featherweight title
trajectory.description: Defeated Jose Aldo at UFC 212 on June 3, 2017 to unify the UFC Featherweight Championship, ending Aldo's long reign.

trajectory.title: Defended title against Ortega
trajectory.description: Successfully defended the featherweight title with a doctor stoppage TKO over Brian Ortega at UFC 231.

trajectory.title: Lost title to Volkanovski
trajectory.description: Lost the UFC featherweight title to Alexander Volkanovski by unanimous decision at UFC 245.

trajectory.title: Won BMF title with iconic knockout
trajectory.description: Knocked out Justin Gaethje at 4:59 of the fifth round at UFC 300 to win the symbolic BMF title in one of the most memorable moments in UFC history.

name: David Benavidez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBC super middleweight world title at age 20 in September 2017, becoming the youngest super middleweight champion in boxing history.
starting_point: Born December 17, 1996 in Phoenix, Arizona to a Mexican father and Ecuadorian mother; father Jose Benavidez Sr. was a boxing trainer who started David in the gym at age 3; struggled with obesity as a teenager, weighing 250 pounds at age 13 before losing over 100 pounds.
current_position: Unified WBA and WBO cruiserweight world champion and WBA/WBC light heavyweight champion; one of boxing's top pound-for-pound fighters with a 31-0 record.

trajectory.title: Professional boxing debut
trajectory.description: Made his professional debut at age 16, defeating Erasmo Moreno by first-round knockout in Puerto Penasco.

trajectory.title: Signed with Sampson Boxing
trajectory.description: Signed a promotional deal with Sampson Lewkowicz's Sampson Boxing and won the NABF Junior light heavyweight title.

trajectory.title: Youngest super middleweight champion
trajectory.description: Defeated Ronald Gavril by split decision in September 2017 to win the vacant WBC super middleweight title, becoming the youngest super middleweight champion in history at age 20.

trajectory.title: Stripped of title after positive drug test
trajectory.description: Was stripped of the WBC title after testing positive for a banned substance, receiving a retroactive suspension.

trajectory.title: Reclaimed WBC super middleweight title
trajectory.description: Regained the WBC super middleweight title by stopping Anthony Dirrell, becoming a two-time world champion.

trajectory.title: Defeated Caleb Plant in mega-fight
trajectory.description: Won a unanimous decision over Caleb Plant in a highly anticipated super middleweight showdown, solidifying his status as the division's best.

trajectory.title: Won WBC light heavyweight title
trajectory.description: Defeated David Morrell Jr. to become the WBC light heavyweight champion, becoming a two-division world champion.

name: Jesse Rodriguez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBC super flyweight world title at age 22 on February 5, 2022 by defeating Carlos Cuadras, becoming the first fighter born in the 2000s to win a world boxing championship.
starting_point: Born January 20, 2000 in San Antonio, Texas; from a boxing family with father and trainer Roberto Rodriguez; trained alongside his brother Joshua Franco, also a world champion boxer.
current_position: Unified WBA, WBC, WBO, and Ring Magazine super flyweight champion; WBA bantamweight champion; one of boxing's top pound-for-pound fighters.

trajectory.title: Professional boxing debut
trajectory.description: Turned professional on March 10, 2017, winning his debut by unanimous decision over Mauricio Cruz.

trajectory.title: Won WBC super flyweight title
trajectory.description: Defeated Carlos Cuadras on February 5, 2022 to win the vacant WBC super flyweight title, becoming the first fighter born in the 2000s to win a world title.

trajectory.title: Defended title with TKO over Sor Rungvisai
trajectory.description: Defended the WBC super flyweight title with an eighth-round TKO of former champion Srisaket Sor Rungvisai in June 2022.

trajectory.title: Unified flyweight titles
trajectory.description: Moved down to flyweight and unified the WBO and IBF titles by defeating Sunny Edwards via ninth-round TKO in December 2023.

trajectory.title: Recaptured WBC super flyweight title
trajectory.description: Returned to super flyweight and knocked out Juan Francisco Estrada in the seventh round to recapture the WBC super flyweight title and the Ring magazine belt.

trajectory.title: Unified super flyweight division
trajectory.description: Added the WBO super flyweight title by stopping Phumelele Cafu, then knocked out Fernando Martinez to add the WBA belt, unifying the super flyweight division.

name: Kosei Tanaka
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBO mini-flyweight world title in 2015 in only his fifth professional fight at approximately age 20, becoming the fastest Japanese fighter to become a world champion.
starting_point: Born June 15, 1995 in Tajimi, Gifu, Japan; trained at the Shirokane Boxing Gym; had a successful amateur career including medals at the World Youth and Asian Youth Championships.
current_position: Retired from boxing in 2024 due to repeated eye injuries; four-weight world champion and one of Japan's greatest boxers.

trajectory.title: Professional boxing debut
trajectory.description: Turned professional at age 18, beginning his career in Japan.

trajectory.title: Won OPBF mini-flyweight title
trajectory.description: Defeated previously unbeaten Ryuji Hara via tenth-round TKO to win the OPBF mini-flyweight title.

trajectory.title: Won WBO mini-flyweight world title
trajectory.description: Defeated Julian Yedras by unanimous decision to win the WBO mini-flyweight title in only his fifth professional fight, setting a Japanese record for fastest world title.

trajectory.title: Won second division title
trajectory.description: Moved up to junior-flyweight and defeated Moises Fuentes by TKO to become a two-weight world champion in just eight fights.

trajectory.title: Won third division title
trajectory.description: Defeated Sho Kimura by majority decision to win the WBO flyweight title, becoming a three-weight world champion in just 12 fights, tied with Vasiliy Lomachenko.

trajectory.title: Won fourth division title and retired
trajectory.description: Won the WBO junior-bantamweight title in February 2024, becoming the fastest male four-division champion at 21 fights, but was forced to retire due to eye injuries.

name: Marc Márquez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 125cc World Championship at age 17 in 2010, then became the youngest MotoGP World Champion in history at age 20 as a rookie in 2013, winning six races in his debut season.
starting_point: Born February 17, 1993 in Lleida, Spain; raised in Cervera, a small town near Lleida; got his first motorcycle at age 4; younger brother Alex Marquez is also a Grand Prix motorcycle racer.
current_position: Racing for Ducati Lenovo Team in MotoGP; nine-time Grand Prix World Champion including seven MotoGP titles, widely considered one of the greatest motorcycle racers of all time.

trajectory.title: 125cc World Championship debut
trajectory.description: Joined the 125cc World Championship at age 15, becoming the youngest rider ever to make a World Championship podium in his sixth race.

trajectory.title: Won 125cc World Championship
trajectory.description: Won the 125cc World Championship at age 17 with 10 race victories, becoming one of the youngest champions in the category.

trajectory.title: Won Moto2 World Championship
trajectory.description: Won the Moto2 World Championship, setting the stage for his promotion to the premier MotoGP class.

trajectory.title: Youngest MotoGP World Champion
trajectory.description: Won the MotoGP World Championship in his rookie season at age 20, becoming the youngest premier-class champion in history and the first rookie champion since 1978.

trajectory.title: Dominant second MotoGP title
trajectory.description: Won his second MotoGP title with 13 victories, including the first 10 races of the season, setting a record for most premier-class wins in a single season.

trajectory.title: Eighth World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his sixth consecutive MotoGP title and eighth World Championship overall, becoming the youngest rider to win eight Grand Prix championships.

trajectory.title: Career-threatening injury
trajectory.description: Crashed at the 2020 season opener in Jerez, breaking his right humerus, and missed the rest of the season after multiple surgeries.

trajectory.title: Ninth World Championship with Ducati
trajectory.description: Won his seventh MotoGP World Championship and ninth overall after moving to Ducati, completing one of the greatest comebacks in motorsport history.

name: Brad Binder
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Moto3 World Championship at age 21 in 2016, becoming the first South African to win a motorcycle Grand Prix world title in decades, and won his first MotoGP race at age 24 in 2020.
starting_point: Born August 11, 1995 in Potchefstroom, South Africa; started in go-karting at age 8, switched to motorcycles at age 10; younger brother Darryn Binder is also a motorcycle racer.
current_position: Racing for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing in MotoGP; the first and only South African to win a MotoGP race.

trajectory.title: Grand Prix debut in 125cc
trajectory.description: Made his Grand Prix debut in the 125cc World Championship as a replacement rider, earning a full-time ride for 2012.

trajectory.title: Joined Red Bull KTM Ajo team
trajectory.description: Signed with the Red Bull KTM Ajo team in Moto3, finishing sixth in the standings with four podiums.

trajectory.title: Won Moto3 World Championship
trajectory.description: Won the Moto3 World Championship with seven victories, becoming the first South African to win a motorcycle Grand Prix world title in decades.

trajectory.title: Moved to Moto2
trajectory.description: Stepped up to Moto2 with Ajo Motorsport, finishing eighth in the championship with three podiums.

trajectory.title: Moto2 runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished second in the Moto2 World Championship with five wins, earning promotion to MotoGP with Red Bull KTM Factory Racing.

trajectory.title: First MotoGP race win
trajectory.description: Won the Czech Republic Grand Prix in his rookie MotoGP season, becoming the first South African and first KTM rider to win a MotoGP race.

trajectory.title: Won Austrian Grand Prix
trajectory.description: Won his second MotoGP race at the Austrian Grand Prix at the Red Bull Ring, finishing sixth in the championship.

name: Chloe Kim
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in snowboard halfpipe at age 17 at the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics, becoming the youngest woman to win an Olympic snowboarding gold medal.
starting_point: Born April 23, 2000 in Long Beach, California to South Korean immigrant parents; grew up in Torrance, California; father quit his job to drive her to Mammoth Mountain every weekend for training; started snowboarding at age 4.
current_position: Two-time Olympic gold medalist and eight-time X Games gold medalist; competing toward the 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics; also a Princeton University student.

trajectory.title: Joined U.S. Snowboarding Team
trajectory.description: Joined the U.S. Snowboarding Team at age 13, marking her entry into elite competition.

trajectory.title: Youngest X Games gold medalist
trajectory.description: Won gold at the Winter X Games superpipe at age 14, becoming the youngest ever X Games gold medalist at the time.

trajectory.title: First woman to land back-to-back 1080s
trajectory.description: Became the first female snowboarder to land back-to-back 1080 spins in competition at the U.S. Snowboarding Grand Prix, scoring a perfect 100.

trajectory.title: Two golds at Winter Youth Olympics
trajectory.description: Won gold in both halfpipe and slopestyle at the Lillehammer Winter Youth Olympic Games, also serving as USA flagbearer.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold at Pyeongchang
trajectory.description: Won gold in women's snowboard halfpipe at the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics at age 17, becoming the youngest woman to win an Olympic snowboarding gold medal.

trajectory.title: Second consecutive Olympic gold
trajectory.description: Won her second consecutive Olympic gold medal in halfpipe at the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, becoming the first woman to win back-to-back halfpipe golds.

trajectory.title: First woman to land 1260 in competition
trajectory.description: Became the first woman to land a 1260-degree spin in competition history, pushing the boundaries of women's snowboarding.

name: Ye Shiwen
milestone_by_age_26: Won two Olympic gold medals at age 16 at the 2012 London Olympics, breaking the world record in the 400m individual medley and the Olympic record in the 200m individual medley.
starting_point: Born March 1, 1996 in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China; father was a runner and mother was a long jump champion; started swimming at age 6 after a kindergarten teacher noticed her large hands and feet; joined the provincial team by 2007 and national team by 2008.
current_position: Chinese competitive swimmer; continued competing through the 2022 Asian Games where she won gold in the 200m breaststroke.

trajectory.title: Asian Games gold medals
trajectory.description: Won gold in both the 200m and 400m individual medley at the 2010 Asian Games in Guangzhou at age 14.

trajectory.title: World Championships gold
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 200m individual medley at the 2011 World Championships in Shanghai, establishing herself as a rising star.

trajectory.title: Two Olympic gold medals at London
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 400m IM (breaking the world record) and the 200m IM (breaking the Olympic record) at the 2012 London Olympics at age 16.

trajectory.title: Short Course World Championship gold
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 200m IM at the Short Course World Championships in Istanbul, adding to her medal haul.

trajectory.title: Asian Games double gold
trajectory.description: Won gold in both the 200m and 400m individual medley at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.

trajectory.title: Competed at Rio Olympics
trajectory.description: Competed at the 2016 Rio Olympics but failed to win any medals, as her times declined from her 2012 peak.

trajectory.title: World Championships silver medals
trajectory.description: Won silver in both the 200m and 400m individual medley at the 2019 World Championships in Gwangju, marking a career resurgence.

trajectory.title: Asian Games gold in breaststroke
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 200m breaststroke at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, demonstrating versatility across events.

name: Letsile Tebogo
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the 200m at age 21 at the 2024 Paris Olympics, earning Botswana's first-ever Olympic gold medal, and won silver in the 100m at the 2023 World Championships at age 20.
starting_point: Born June 7, 2003 in the village of Kanye, about 83 kilometers southwest of Botswana's capital Gaborone; grew up playing football and sprinting; focused on track after football injuries; mother Seratiwa was a major inspiration who died in May 2024.
current_position: Olympic 200m champion and Botswana's first Olympic gold medalist; ranked #2 in the world in the 200m; competing on the Diamond League circuit.

trajectory.title: World U20 Championships gold
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 100m at the 2021 World Athletics U20 Championships in Nairobi, becoming the first Botswana athlete to win 100m gold at any World Championships level.

trajectory.title: Broke 10-second barrier
trajectory.description: Became the first man from Botswana to break the 10-second barrier in the 100m, clocking 9.96 at the Gaborone International Meet, setting a world U20 record.

trajectory.title: World U20 100m record
trajectory.description: Improved his own world U20 100m record to 9.91 seconds at the World U20 Championships in Cali, Colombia.

trajectory.title: World Championships silver and bronze
trajectory.description: Won silver in the 100m and bronze in the 200m at the 2023 World Athletics Championships in Budapest, becoming Africa's first world 100m medallist.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold in 200m
trajectory.description: Won gold in the 200m at the 2024 Paris Olympics in 19.46 seconds, earning Botswana's first-ever Olympic gold medal and the first African to win the Olympic 200m.

trajectory.title: Olympic silver in 4x400m relay
trajectory.description: Won silver as part of Botswana's 4x400m relay team at the Paris Olympics, two days after his individual gold.

name: Alexis Barreyat
milestone_by_age_26: Founded and launched BeReal, a photo-sharing social app, in early 2020 at age 24, which later reached #1 on Apple's App Store and was named iPhone App of the Year 2022.
starting_point: Born in France; attended 42 born2code coding school in Paris from 2013 to 2016; worked in media production at GoPro in Munich from 2016 to 2018 before founding BeReal.
current_position: Stepped down as CEO of BeReal after its acquisition by Voodoo in June 2024; based in Paris, France.

trajectory.title: Attended 42 coding school
trajectory.description: Enrolled at 42 born2code, a tuition-free coding school in Paris, developing programming skills from July 2013 to March 2016.

trajectory.title: Joined GoPro in media production
trajectory.description: Worked in media production at GoPro in Munich from March 2016 to December 2018, gaining experience in content creation.

trajectory.title: Co-founded BeReal
trajectory.description: Co-founded BeReal with Kevin Perreau in late 2019, beginning development of a social media app focused on authentic, unfiltered sharing.

trajectory.title: Launched BeReal on App Store
trajectory.description: Launched BeReal on the App Store in early 2020, initially gaining traction on French college campuses and reaching 500K users by 2021.

trajectory.title: Raised $30M Series A
trajectory.description: Raised $30 million in funding led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel as BeReal began expanding beyond France.

trajectory.title: BeReal went viral globally
trajectory.description: BeReal went viral in 2022, reaching #1 on Apple's App Store and being named iPhone App of the Year, prompting Instagram and TikTok to launch similar features.

trajectory.title: BeReal acquired by Voodoo
trajectory.description: BeReal was acquired by Voodoo in June 2024, with Barreyat stepping down as CEO to be replaced by Aymeric Roffe.

name: Hayden Adams
milestone_by_age_26: Created and launched Uniswap, a decentralized exchange protocol on Ethereum, deploying it to the Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018 at age 26, which became one of the most important protocols in DeFi.
starting_point: Born and raised in the New York area; graduated from Stony Brook University with a bachelor's in engineering in 2016; worked as a mechanical engineer at Siemens before being laid off in 2017, which led him to learn coding and enter crypto.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Uniswap Labs; Uniswap has surpassed $1 trillion in lifetime trading volume and is one of the most important protocols in DeFi.

trajectory.title: Graduated and joined Siemens
trajectory.description: Graduated from Stony Brook University with an engineering degree and began working at Siemens performing engineering simulations.

trajectory.title: Laid off from Siemens, learned to code
trajectory.description: Was laid off from Siemens in mid-2017 and began learning to code, introduced to Ethereum by friend Karl Floersch.

trajectory.title: Built Uniswap prototype
trajectory.description: Built a prototype of Uniswap based on Vitalik Buterin's concept of an automated market maker, presenting it at conferences worldwide.

trajectory.title: Launched Uniswap on Ethereum mainnet
trajectory.description: Deployed Uniswap to the Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018, creating the first major decentralized exchange protocol.

trajectory.title: Launched Uniswap V2 and UNI token
trajectory.description: Launched Uniswap V2 and the UNI governance token, with Uniswap surpassing Coinbase Pro in daily trading volume.

trajectory.title: Uniswap surpassed $1T volume
trajectory.description: Uniswap surpassed $1 trillion in lifetime trading volume, cementing its position as the leading decentralized exchange.

trajectory.title: Launched Uniswap V4
trajectory.description: Launched Uniswap V4, introducing hooks and custom pool features, further expanding the protocol's capabilities.

name: Joey Krug
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Augur, one of the first decentralized prediction market protocols on Ethereum, in 2014 at age 19, and organized the first ICO on Ethereum in 2015, raising $5.7 million at age 20.
starting_point: Born and raised in the small farming town of Knoxville, Illinois; started programming in Applesoft BASIC in middle school after his father bought him an Apple II GS on eBay; studied Computer Science at Pomona College before dropping out.
current_position: Partner at Founders Fund focused on crypto strategy; co-founder of Augur and Eco; based in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Started Bitcoin mining
trajectory.description: Began mining Bitcoin in high school while building vintage hardware with his father.

trajectory.title: Built Bitcoin POS system
trajectory.description: Built a Bitcoin point-of-sale payment system and briefly worked as a game developer before founding MariPoS.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Augur
trajectory.description: Co-founded the Forecast Foundation, the organization behind Augur, a decentralized prediction market protocol on Ethereum.

trajectory.title: First ICO on Ethereum
trajectory.description: Organized the first ICO on Ethereum, raising $5.7 million for Augur, a landmark event in crypto fundraising.

trajectory.title: Joined Pantera Capital as co-CIO
trajectory.description: Became co-chief investment officer at Pantera Capital, one of the largest blockchain-focused investment firms, leading investments in Starkware, Arbitrum, and Alchemy.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Eco
trajectory.description: Co-founded Eco, a platform for spending, saving, and sending money using blockchain technology.

trajectory.title: Joined Founders Fund as Partner
trajectory.description: Joined Peter Thiel's Founders Fund as a Partner in April 2023, focusing on defining the firm's crypto investment strategy.

name: David Hsu
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Retool in January 2017 at age 25, went through Y Combinator's Winter 2017 batch, raised $1.5 million, and grew Retool to $2M in ARR by August 2018 at age 26, later building it to a $3.2 billion valuation.
starting_point: Born in Silicon Valley to Chinese immigrant parents who came to the U.S. for post-graduate studies; grew up in Palo Alto; rebellious teenager who was moved to Saratoga to refocus; graduated from Oxford University with a degree in Philosophy and Computer Science.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Retool, valued at $3.2 billion with customers including Amazon, DoorDash, and the NFL; based in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Oxford University
trajectory.description: Graduated from the University of Oxford with a degree in Philosophy and Computer Science.

trajectory.title: Founded Retool after pivot
trajectory.description: Founded Retool in January 2017 after pivoting from a failing UK-based Venmo competitor called Cashew, which went through YC's Winter 2017 batch.

trajectory.title: Y Combinator Winter 2017 batch
trajectory.description: Presented at YC Demo Day with Retool, announcing a $1.5M enterprise customer pilot.

trajectory.title: Launched on Hacker News, reached $2M ARR
trajectory.description: Posted Retool on Hacker News in August 2018, shifting to inbound demand and reaching $2M in ARR with 5-20 companies signing up daily.

trajectory.title: Retool valued at $3.2 billion
trajectory.description: Retool reached a $3.2 billion valuation after raising funding rounds with customers including Amazon, DoorDash, and the NFL.

name: Lisa Sauermann
milestone_by_age_26: Won four gold medals (2008-2011) and one silver medal (2007) at the International Mathematical Olympiad, achieving the single highest perfect score in 2011 at age 18.
starting_point: Born September 25, 1992 in Dresden, Saxony, Germany; attended a special school for mathematics in Dresden; sister Anne was also a successful math and science Olympiad participant.
current_position: Professor of Mathematics at the University of Bonn, holding a tenured chair professorship in probabilistic combinatorics.

trajectory.title: IMO silver medal
trajectory.description: Won a silver medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad representing Germany, her first of five IMO appearances.

trajectory.title: First IMO gold medal
trajectory.description: Won her first gold medal at the IMO, beginning a streak of four consecutive gold medals.

trajectory.title: IMO gold with near-perfect score
trajectory.description: Won her second gold medal at the IMO, scoring 41 out of 42 points and ranking third overall.

trajectory.title: Perfect score at IMO
trajectory.description: Achieved a perfect score of 42 at the IMO, the single highest score in the competition, winning her fourth gold medal.

trajectory.title: Completed bachelor's at University of Bonn
trajectory.description: Completed her bachelor's thesis on algebraic geometry under Michael Rapoport at the University of Bonn.

trajectory.title: PhD from Stanford University
trajectory.description: Earned her PhD from Stanford University under Jacob Fox, with a dissertation titled 'Modern Methods in Extremal Combinatorics,' winning two dissertation prizes.

trajectory.title: Assistant professor at MIT
trajectory.description: Became an assistant professor at MIT and received the European Prize in Combinatorics for her work in combinatorics.

trajectory.title: Tenured professorship at University of Bonn
trajectory.description: Accepted a tenured chair professorship at the University of Bonn, returning to Germany after nine years in the United States.

name: Chloe Gong
milestone_by_age_26: Debut novel These Violent Delights became a New York Times bestseller in November 2020 at age 21, making her one of the youngest YA hardcover bestseller authors.
starting_point: Born December 16, 1998 in Shanghai, China; moved to New Zealand with her family at age 2; raised on the North Shore in Auckland, New Zealand; attended Rangitoto College; began writing books at age 13 using the Notes app on her iPad.
current_position: #1 New York Times bestselling author based in New York City; named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2024; books published in over 20 countries.

trajectory.title: Wrote These Violent Delights
trajectory.description: Wrote her debut novel These Violent Delights after her freshman year at the University of Pennsylvania, a Romeo and Juliet-inspired story set in 1920s Shanghai.

trajectory.title: Signed with literary agent
trajectory.description: Signed with a literary agent at age 19 while still an undergraduate at the University of Pennsylvania.

trajectory.title: New York Times bestseller
trajectory.description: These Violent Delights became a New York Times bestseller in November 2020, making her one of the youngest YA hardcover bestseller authors.

trajectory.title: Published sequel and graduated
trajectory.description: Published the sequel Our Violent Ends in November 2021 and graduated from the University of Pennsylvania with a double major in English and International Relations.

trajectory.title: Won Sir Julius Vogel Award
trajectory.description: Won the Best Youth Novel at the 2021 Sir Julius Vogel Awards for These Violent Delights.

trajectory.title: Published Immortal Longings
trajectory.description: Published Immortal Longings, the first book in a new adult fantasy series, further expanding her publishing career.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2024 for her achievements as a bestselling author with books published in over 20 countries.

name: Faridah Àbíké-Íyímídé
milestone_by_age_26: Landed a seven-figure (million-dollar) book deal with Macmillan for her debut novel Ace of Spades in September 2020 at age 21, while still a university student.
starting_point: Born and raised in Croydon, South London, England; from a working-class background; Muslim family; attended a working-class school in South London before studying at the University of Aberdeen in Scotland.
current_position: New York Times bestselling author of Ace of Spades, Where Sleeping Girls Lie, and Four Eids and a Funeral; named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2026; based in London.

trajectory.title: Began writing Ace of Spades
trajectory.description: Began writing Ace of Spades during her first year at the University of Aberdeen, inspired by Gossip Girl but with more Black representation.

trajectory.title: Gained agent and UK book deal
trajectory.description: Gained a literary agent and a UK book deal with Usborne Publishing for Ace of Spades.

trajectory.title: Founded Avengers of Colour
trajectory.description: Founded Avengers of Colour, a mentorship initiative for un-agented writers of colour aimed at supporting publication opportunities.

trajectory.title: Seven-figure US book deal
trajectory.description: Landed a seven-figure (million-dollar) book deal with Macmillan Publishers in the US for Ace of Spades and a second novel.

trajectory.title: Ace of Spades published to acclaim
trajectory.description: Ace of Spades was published in June 2021, reaching the top ten on the New York Times Best Seller list and winning the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Literary Work for Youth/Teens.

trajectory.title: Morris Award finalist
trajectory.description: Named a finalist for the William C. Morris Award for Ace of Spades, recognizing a debut book published for young adults.

trajectory.title: Published multiple new novels
trajectory.description: Published Where Sleeping Girls Lie and Four Eids and a Funeral, and wrote stories for Marvel's Spider-Verse and BBC's Doctor Who.

name: Dara McAnulty
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2020 Wainwright Prize for UK Nature Writing for his debut book Diary of a Young Naturalist at age 16, becoming the youngest ever winner of a major UK literary prize.
starting_point: Born March 31, 2004 in Northern Ireland; from a family where he, his mother, and his two siblings are all autistic; his father was a conservationist; grew up in Belfast before moving to the countryside at age 9, where nature became his sanctuary.
current_position: Award-winning author and naturalist from Northern Ireland; awarded a BEM in 2022; continues writing and environmental campaigning.

trajectory.title: Started wildlife blog
trajectory.description: Started his wildlife blog 'Young Fermanagh Naturalist' at age 12 to share his observations about nature, which grew rapidly in popularity.

trajectory.title: Points of Light recognition
trajectory.description: Was celebrated in the UK government's 'Points of Light' program at age 14 for his work connecting young people to nature.

trajectory.title: Youngest RSPB Medal recipient
trajectory.description: Became the youngest ever recipient of the RSPB Medal for conservation at age 15.

trajectory.title: Published Diary of a Young Naturalist
trajectory.description: Published his debut book Diary of a Young Naturalist in May 2020, chronicling his 14th year as an autistic teenager connected to the natural world.

trajectory.title: Won Wainwright Prize
trajectory.description: Won the 2020 Wainwright Prize for UK Nature Writing, becoming the youngest ever winner of a major UK literary prize.

trajectory.title: Won British Book Award
trajectory.description: Won the British Book Award for Narrative Non-Fiction Book of the Year for Diary of a Young Naturalist.

trajectory.title: Awarded BEM
trajectory.description: Became the youngest recipient on King Charles III's first New Year's Honours List, awarded a BEM for services to nature and the autistic community.

trajectory.title: Published Wild Child
trajectory.description: Published his second book Wild Child, A Journey Through Nature, aimed at connecting young readers with the natural world.

name: Lauren Roberts
milestone_by_age_26: Self-published debut novel Powerless in November 2023 at age 21, which became a New York Times bestseller and led to a deal with Simon & Schuster; the series has sold over 4 million copies.
starting_point: Born and raised in Michigan; started a BookTok account at age 16; came up with the idea for Powerless at age 18 while in college; dropped out of college to focus on writing.
current_position: New York Times bestselling author of the Powerless series with over 4 million copies sold; a TV adaptation is underway; based in Michigan.

trajectory.title: Started BookTok account
trajectory.description: Launched a BookTok account at age 16 focused on romantasy books, building a social media following.

trajectory.title: Conceived and wrote Powerless
trajectory.description: Came up with the idea for Powerless on a livestream and spent three months writing the novel while juggling college and a part-time job.

trajectory.title: Self-published Powerless
trajectory.description: Self-published Powerless in November 2023 through Amazon's Kindle Direct Publishing and Barnes & Noble Press after hiring a freelance editor.

trajectory.title: Signed with Simon & Schuster
trajectory.description: Signed a deal with Simon & Schuster, which republished Powerless; the book stayed on the New York Times bestseller list for 34 weeks.

trajectory.title: Published Reckless sequel
trajectory.description: Published Reckless, the sequel to Powerless, in July 2024, continuing the bestselling romantasy trilogy.

trajectory.title: Published Fearless and TV deal
trajectory.description: Published Fearless, the final book in the Powerless trilogy, with the series having sold over 4 million copies and a TV adaptation underway.

name: Leila Mottley
milestone_by_age_26: Published debut novel Nightcrawling in June 2022 at age 19, which became a New York Times bestseller, an Oprah Book Club pick, and was longlisted for the Booker Prize, making her the youngest author ever nominated.
starting_point: Born in 2002 or 2003 in Oakland, California; father is a playwright; grew up in a literary and creative family; raised in Oakland where she continues to live; attended Smith College before taking indefinite leave to pursue writing.
current_position: Author and poet based in Oakland, California; published her sophomore novel The Girls Who Grew Big in June 2025.

trajectory.title: Vice Youth Poet Laureate of Oakland
trajectory.description: Served as Vice Youth Poet Laureate of Oakland, California, beginning her public literary career as a teenager.

trajectory.title: Oakland Youth Poet Laureate
trajectory.description: Named the 2018 Oakland Youth Poet Laureate at age 16, after two years as runner-up, gaining recognition for her poetry.

trajectory.title: Wrote Nightcrawling manuscript
trajectory.description: Wrote the first draft of Nightcrawling during the summer after graduating high school, completing it within three months.

trajectory.title: Published Nightcrawling
trajectory.description: Published her debut novel Nightcrawling in June 2022 with Knopf, which became a New York Times bestseller and an Oprah Book Club pick.

trajectory.title: Longlisted for Booker Prize
trajectory.description: Nightcrawling was longlisted for the Booker Prize, making Mottley the youngest author ever nominated for the award.

trajectory.title: Published poetry collection
trajectory.description: Published her poetry collection 'woke up no light,' expanding her literary output beyond novels.

trajectory.title: Published The Girls Who Grew Big
trajectory.description: Published her sophomore novel The Girls Who Grew Big in June 2025, further establishing her literary career.

name: Tillie Walden
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2018 Eisner Award for Best Reality-Based Work for her graphic memoir Spinning at age 22, making her one of the youngest Eisner Award winners ever. She had already published three graphic novels by age 20.
starting_point: Born in 1996 in San Diego, California; grew up in New Jersey and Austin, Texas; was a competitive figure skater; named after her paternal grandmother, an artist who died before she was born; father encouraged her with comics and manga.
current_position: Cartoonist and professor at the Center for Cartoon Studies in Vermont; named Vermont's cartoonist laureate for 2023-2026, the state's youngest ever.

trajectory.title: Published debut graphic novel
trajectory.description: Published her first graphic novel The End of Summer with Avery Hill Publishing while still a student at the Center for Cartoon Studies.

trajectory.title: Won two Ignatz Awards
trajectory.description: Won two Ignatz Awards for Outstanding Artist and Promising New Talent, recognizing her early graphic novellas.

trajectory.title: Published Spinning
trajectory.description: Published Spinning, a graphic memoir about her years as a competitive figure skater and her coming out, with First Second Books.

trajectory.title: Won Eisner Award for Spinning
trajectory.description: Won the 2018 Eisner Award for Best Reality-Based Work for Spinning, becoming one of the youngest Eisner Award winners ever.

trajectory.title: Published On a Sunbeam
trajectory.description: Published On a Sunbeam, a sci-fi graphic novel that earned critical acclaim and won the LA Times Book Prize in 2019.

trajectory.title: Second Eisner Award
trajectory.description: Won her second Eisner Award for Best Graphic Album-New for Are You Listening?, cementing her status as a leading cartoonist.

trajectory.title: Published Clementine
trajectory.description: Published Clementine, the first installment in a graphic novel series set in Robert Kirkman's The Walking Dead universe.

trajectory.title: Named Vermont's cartoonist laureate
trajectory.description: Named Vermont's fifth cartoonist laureate for 2023-2026, becoming the youngest artist to receive the honor.

name: Emerson Spartz
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored MuggleNet.com's What Will Happen in Harry Potter 7 in fall 2006 at age 19, which spent 26 weeks on the New York Times Children's Bestseller List, peaking at #2 and selling 350,000 copies. He had already built MuggleNet into the #1 Harry Potter fan site with 50 million monthly pageviews by his teens.
starting_point: Born February 17, 1987 in LaPorte, Indiana; parents Tom and Maggi Spartz allowed him to homeschool himself at age 12, where he developed his own curriculum and read daily biographies of successful people from Investor's Business Daily.
current_position: Founder of Dose (formerly Spartz Media), a digital media company; based in Chicago; named to Forbes and Inc 30 Under 30 lists.

trajectory.title: Founded MuggleNet
trajectory.description: Founded MuggleNet, a Harry Potter fan website, at age 12 using a WYSIWYG site builder, growing it into the #1 Harry Potter fan site with 50 million monthly pageviews.

trajectory.title: NYT bestselling author
trajectory.description: Co-authored MuggleNet.com's What Will Happen in Harry Potter 7, which spent 26 weeks on the NYT Children's Bestseller List, peaking at #2 and selling 350,000 copies.

trajectory.title: Six-figure income from MuggleNet
trajectory.description: Was earning a six-figure income from MuggleNet with six paid and 120 volunteer staff by 2007.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Notre Dame
trajectory.description: Graduated from the University of Notre Dame's Mendoza College of Business with a BBA degree.

trajectory.title: Founded Spartz Media
trajectory.description: Founded Spartz Media (later Dose), a viral media company that created 20+ viral content sites including OMG Facts, attracting 50 million visitors monthly.

trajectory.title: Dose raised $35M in funding
trajectory.description: Dose raised $35 million in funding and expanded into video content generating billions of views, with a broadcast TV show on CW stations.

name: Aneesh Chaganty
milestone_by_age_26: His feature directorial debut Searching premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 21, 2018, winning the Alfred P. Sloan Feature Film Prize and the Best of NEXT! Audience Award, and was acquired by Sony Pictures Worldwide.
starting_point: Born in 1991 or 1992 in Redmond, Washington; attended the University of Southern California for film; of Indian-American heritage.
current_position: Film director and screenwriter based in Los Angeles; directed Searching, Run, and produced the sequel Missing.

trajectory.title: Seeds short film went viral
trajectory.description: His two-minute Google Glass short film Seeds garnered over 1 million YouTube views in 24 hours, becoming an internet sensation.

trajectory.title: Joined Google Creative Lab
trajectory.description: Was invited to join the Google 5 team at Google Creative Lab in New York City, spending two years writing and directing Google commercials including a Super Bowl ad.

trajectory.title: Searching premiered at Sundance
trajectory.description: His feature directorial debut Searching premiered at Sundance on January 21, 2018, winning the Alfred P. Sloan Feature Film Prize and the Best of NEXT! Audience Award.

trajectory.title: Searching acquired by Sony Pictures
trajectory.description: Searching was acquired by Sony Pictures for worldwide distribution and grossed over $75 million at the box office.

trajectory.title: Released Run on Hulu
trajectory.description: His second film Run, starring Sarah Paulson, was released on Hulu and became the platform's most-watched feature title ever during its opening weekend.

trajectory.title: Produced Missing
trajectory.description: Produced Missing, an anthology sequel to Searching, which was released theatrically and continued the screenlife thriller franchise.

name: Kane Parsons
milestone_by_age_26: Created the viral Backrooms found-footage web series on YouTube in January 2022 at age 16, amassing 78+ million views and leading to an A24 feature film deal as their youngest-ever director.
starting_point: Born June 18, 2005 in Petaluma, California; father Michael Parsons is a British visual effects artist; mother is a therapist; parents divorced when he was 7; developed arthritis at age 13, which limited his mobility and led him to focus on VFX and filmmaking.
current_position: Film director and YouTuber; directed A24's Backrooms feature film at age 20, becoming the youngest director in A24's history; based in Vancouver.

trajectory.title: Attack on Titan fan films
trajectory.description: Created animated short fan films adapting Attack on Titan in the style of historical war photography, praised for their horror elements and faithfulness to the series.

trajectory.title: Created Backrooms web series
trajectory.description: Released The Backrooms (Found Footage) on YouTube on January 7, 2022 at age 16, which went viral and amassed 78+ million views, spawning a 24-installment web series.

trajectory.title: Signed with A24 for feature film
trajectory.description: Received studio offers while still in high school and signed with A24 to direct a feature film adaptation of the Backrooms, becoming their youngest-ever director.

trajectory.title: Delayed college for filmmaking
trajectory.description: Decided to delay college to pursue his filmmaking career with A24, focusing on the Backrooms feature film.

trajectory.title: Backrooms feature film released
trajectory.description: A24's Backrooms feature film was released to critical and commercial success, with Parsons becoming the youngest director to have a film debut at #1 at both domestic and global box offices, grossing over $333 million worldwide.

name: Jason Fuchs
milestone_by_age_26: Made his feature screenwriting debut with Ice Age: Continental Drift in July 2012 at age 26; the film grossed $877 million worldwide, making it the fifth highest-grossing film of 2012.
starting_point: Born in New York City; began acting as a child, appearing in films and television shows including Flipper and The Guiding Light before transitioning to screenwriting.
current_position: Screenwriter and producer based in Los Angeles; wrote Wonder Woman (2017) and the upcoming Ballerina; continues working on major studio franchises.

trajectory.title: Child acting career
trajectory.description: Began acting as a child, appearing in films like Flipper (1996) and on television shows including The Guiding Light.

trajectory.title: Feature screenwriting debut with Ice Age 4
trajectory.description: Made his feature screenwriting debut with Ice Age: Continental Drift, which grossed $877 million worldwide and became the fifth highest-grossing film of 2012.

trajectory.title: Wrote Wonder Woman
trajectory.description: Co-wrote the screenplay for Wonder Woman (2017), starring Gal Gadot, which grossed over $822 million worldwide and was a critical and commercial success.

trajectory.title: Sold Ballerina spec script
trajectory.description: Sold his spec script Ballerina to Lionsgate in a bidding war, which was later retrofitted into a John Wick spinoff film.

trajectory.title: Ballerina film released
trajectory.description: The John Wick spinoff Ballerina, based on his spec script, was released as a major studio production.

name: Shay Hatten
milestone_by_age_26: Sold his spec script Ballerina to Lionsgate in 2017 at age 23 in a bidding war, which was retrofitted into a John Wick spinoff; his earlier script Maximum King! made the 2016 Black List.
starting_point: Born in approximately 1994; attended film school; developed an interest in screenwriting from a young age.
current_position: Screenwriter based in Los Angeles; wrote the John Wick spinoff Ballerina and co-wrote Army of the Dead for Zack Snyder.

trajectory.title: Maximum King! made the Black List
trajectory.description: His script Maximum King! was included on the 2016 Black List, Hollywood's annual list of the most-liked unproduced screenplays.

trajectory.title: Sold Ballerina spec script
trajectory.description: Sold his spec script Ballerina to Lionsgate in 2017 in a bidding war at age 23, which was later retrofitted into a John Wick spinoff.

trajectory.title: Wrote Army of the Dead
trajectory.description: Co-wrote the screenplay for Zack Snyder's Army of the Dead (2021), a Netflix zombie heist film.

trajectory.title: Army of the Dead released
trajectory.description: Army of the Dead was released on Netflix, becoming one of the platform's most-watched films.

trajectory.title: Ballerina film released
trajectory.description: The John Wick spinoff Ballerina, based on his spec script sold at age 23, was released as a major theatrical production.

name: Jak Knight
milestone_by_age_26: Became a writer and voice actor on Netflix's animated series 'Big Mouth' starting in 2017 at age 23, and appeared in a half-hour Netflix stand-up special in 2018 as part of the Comedy Lineup series at age 24.
starting_point: Born November 6, 1993 in Seattle, Washington; began performing stand-up comedy as a teenager in Los Angeles clubs; inspired by Dave Chappelle and The Boondocks.
current_position: Died on July 14, 2022 at age 28 in Los Angeles, California; final role was in Chelsea Peretti's film First Time Female Director (posthumous release 2023).

trajectory.title: First industry writing job
trajectory.description: Got his first job in the industry as a writer on the animated Lucas Bros. Moving Co. at around age 20, after being discovered by the Lucas brothers.

trajectory.title: Acting debut in LieGuys
trajectory.description: Appeared in the 2014 movie LieGuys as an iPhone cameraman in his debut acting role.

trajectory.title: Joined Big Mouth as writer and voice actor
trajectory.description: Became a writer and voice actor on Netflix's animated series Big Mouth, voicing the character of DeVon, a role he held until his death.

trajectory.title: Netflix stand-up special
trajectory.description: Appeared in a half-hour Netflix stand-up special as part of the Comedy Lineup series, gaining wider recognition for his comedy.

trajectory.title: Writer and co-executive producer on Pause with Sam Jay
trajectory.description: Worked as a writer, co-executive producer, and actor on the HBO series Pause with Sam Jay, expanding his television career.

trajectory.title: Co-created and starred in Bust Down
trajectory.description: Co-created, executive produced, and starred in the Peacock comedy series Bust Down alongside Chris Redd, Sam Jay, and Langston Kerman, which debuted in March 2022.

trajectory.title: Died at age 28
trajectory.description: Died on July 14, 2022 in Los Angeles, California at age 28, with his final film role in First Time Female Director released posthumously in 2023.

name: Guillaume Diop
milestone_by_age_26: Promoted to étoile (star dancer) at the Paris Opera Ballet on March 11, 2023 at age 23, becoming the first Black dancer to reach the highest rank in the company's 354-year history.
starting_point: Born in Paris, France; trained at the Paris Opera Ballet School, entering the company's rigorous hierarchical system as a young dancer.
current_position: Étoile (star dancer) at the Paris Opera Ballet; the first Black dancer to hold the highest rank in the company's history.

trajectory.title: Joined Paris Opera Ballet
trajectory.description: Joined the Paris Opera Ballet as a member of the corps de ballet after training at the Paris Opera Ballet School.

trajectory.title: Promoted to coryphée
trajectory.description: Was promoted to coryphée, advancing within the Paris Opera Ballet's hierarchical ranking system.

trajectory.title: Promoted to sujet
trajectory.description: Was promoted to sujet, continuing his rapid ascent through the ranks of the Paris Opera Ballet.

trajectory.title: Promoted to premier danseur
trajectory.description: Was promoted to premier danseur, the second-highest rank in the Paris Opera Ballet.

trajectory.title: Named étoile - first Black dancer

trajectory.title: Joined Paris Opera Ballet

trajectory.description: Was promoted to coryphée within the Paris Opera Ballet's hierarchical ranking system.

name: Hannah O'Neill
milestone_by_age_26: Promoted to première danseuse (first soloist) at the Paris Opera Ballet on January 1, 2016 at age 23, the second-highest rank in the company, after winning the internal promotion contest.
starting_point: Born January 8, 1993 in Tokyo, Japan to a Japanese mother and New Zealand father (a professional rugby player); started dancing at age 3 at Kishibe Ballet Studio in Tokyo; moved to Auckland at age 8; trained at the Australian Ballet School in Melbourne from age 15.
current_position: Étoile (star dancer) at the Paris Opera Ballet; the first Japanese dancer to reach the principal-level rank in the company's history.

trajectory.title: Won Prix de Lausanne
trajectory.description: Won the Prix de Lausanne, the world's most prestigious competition for young dancers, representing the Australian Ballet School.

trajectory.title: Won Youth America Grand Prix
trajectory.description: Won first place in the senior women's section at the Youth America Grand Prix in New York.

trajectory.title: Joined Paris Opera Ballet
trajectory.description: Passed the Paris Opera Ballet's external audition and was accepted into the corps de ballet with a seasonal contract, graduating as dux of the Australian Ballet School.

trajectory.title: Offered lifetime contract
trajectory.description: Succeeded in the external audition again and was offered a lifetime contract with the Paris Opera Ballet, becoming a regular member.

trajectory.title: Promoted to coryphée and won Varna silver
trajectory.description: Was promoted to coryphée and won a silver medal at the Varna International Ballet Competition and the Prix du Cercle Carpeaux.

trajectory.title: Promoted to sujet
trajectory.description: Was promoted to sujet, continuing her rapid ascent through the ranks of the Paris Opera Ballet.

trajectory.title: Promoted to première danseuse
trajectory.description: Was promoted to première danseuse (first soloist) on January 1, 2016, the second-highest rank in the Paris Opera Ballet, after winning the internal promotion contest.

trajectory.title: Won Prix Benois de la Danse
trajectory.description: Was named best female dancer at the Benois de la Danse competition in Moscow, one of the world's most prestigious ballet awards.

trajectory.title: Named étoile
trajectory.description: Was named Danseuse Étoile on March 2, 2023, following a performance of Balanchine's Ballet impérial, becoming the first Japanese dancer to reach the highest rank in the Paris Opera Ballet.

name: Erika Henningsen
milestone_by_age_26: Originated the role of Cady Heron in the Tony-nominated Broadway musical Mean Girls, which opened on April 8, 2018 at the August Wilson Theatre when she was 25.
starting_point: Born August 13, 1992 in Moraga, California; youngest of three daughters; started in theatre at age 7 after reciting a poem to an audience; cast in a local production of Grey Gardens at age 14; graduated from the University of Michigan with a BFA in musical theatre in 2014.
current_position: Broadway actress and singer based in New York City; currently starring as Sandra Dee in Just in Time on Broadway; voices Charlie Morningstar in Hazbin Hotel.

trajectory.title: Graduated from University of Michigan
trajectory.description: Graduated from the University of Michigan with a BFA in musical theatre, winning the Alan Eisenberg Award Scholarship for outstanding talent.

trajectory.title: Broadway debut as Fantine in Les Misérables
trajectory.description: Made her Broadway debut as Fantine in Les Misérables, becoming the youngest actress to play the role on Broadway.

trajectory.title: Cast as Cady Heron in Mean Girls
trajectory.description: Was cast as Cady Heron in the Broadway-bound Tina Fey musical Mean Girls, premiering at the National Theatre in Washington, D.C.

trajectory.title: Originated Cady Heron on Broadway
trajectory.description: Originated the role of Cady Heron in the Tony-nominated Broadway musical Mean Girls, which opened on April 8, 2018 at the August Wilson Theatre.

trajectory.title: Outer Critics Circle Award nomination
trajectory.description: Received an Outer Critics Circle Award nomination for Outstanding Actress in a Musical for her performance in Mean Girls.

trajectory.title: Starred in Flying Over Sunset on Broadway
trajectory.description: Appeared in the Lincoln Center Theatre's original Broadway production of Flying Over Sunset.

trajectory.title: Voices Charlie Morningstar in Hazbin Hotel
trajectory.description: Began voicing the lead role of Charlie Morningstar in the popular Amazon animated musical series Hazbin Hotel.

name: Celia Rose Gooding
milestone_by_age_26: Originated the lead role of Frankie Healy in the Broadway musical Jagged Little Pill, which opened in November 2019 at age 19, and received a 2020 Tony Award nomination for Best Featured Actress in a Musical at age 20.
starting_point: Born February 22, 2000 in New York City; mother is Tony-winning Broadway actress LaChanze; grew up immersed in theater; began studying Child Psychology and Musical Theatre at Pace University before dropping out to pursue Broadway.
current_position: Actor and singer; stars as Nyota Uhura in Paramount+'s Star Trek: Strange New Worlds; based in New York.

trajectory.title: Cast in Jagged Little Pill reading
trajectory.description: Was cast in the first 29-hour reading of Jagged Little Pill at age 17, an original musical based on the music of Alanis Morissette.

trajectory.title: World premiere at American Repertory Theatre
trajectory.description: Participated in the world premiere of Jagged Little Pill at the American Repertory Theatre in Cambridge, Massachusetts in May 2018.

trajectory.title: Broadway debut in Jagged Little Pill
trajectory.description: Originated the lead role of Frankie Healy in Jagged Little Pill on Broadway, which opened in November 2019 at the Broadhurst Theatre.

trajectory.title: Mother-daughter Broadway first
trajectory.description: Made history as half of the first mother-daughter duo to perform on Broadway simultaneously, with mother LaChanze in A Christmas Carol.

trajectory.title: Tony Award nomination
trajectory.description: Received a 2020 Tony Award nomination for Best Featured Actress in a Musical for Jagged Little Pill, becoming one of the youngest nominees in the category.

trajectory.title: Won Grammy Award
trajectory.description: Won the 2021 Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album for the Jagged Little Pill original cast recording.

trajectory.title: Cast in Star Trek: Strange New Worlds
trajectory.description: Was cast as Nyota Uhura in the Paramount+ series Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, expanding from Broadway to television.

name: Hailey Kilgore
milestone_by_age_26: Nominated for the 2018 Tony Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role in a Musical at age 19 for her Broadway debut as Ti Moune in the revival of Once on This Island, becoming one of the youngest nominees in the category.
starting_point: Born in 1999 in Humble, Texas; adopted at birth by Rebecca and Eric Kilgore of Portland, Oregon; grew up in Happy Valley, Oregon; competed in pageants from age 9; attended the American Musical and Dramatic Academy in New York.
current_position: Tony-nominated actress and singer; stars as Jukebox in Starz's Power Book III: Raising Kanan; currently starring as Eurydice in Broadway's Hadestown; based in New York.

trajectory.title: Professional theatrical debut
trajectory.description: Made her professional theatrical debut as Rebecca Gibbs in Portland Center Stage's production of Our Town, and appeared in Ain't Misbehavin' the same year.

trajectory.title: Broadway debut in Once on This Island
trajectory.description: Made her Broadway debut as Ti Moune in the revival of Once on This Island at the Circle in the Square Theatre while a first-year student at AMDA.

trajectory.title: Tony Award nomination
trajectory.description: Was nominated for the 2018 Tony Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role in a Musical for Once on This Island, becoming one of the youngest nominees in the category.

trajectory.title: Won Theatre World Award
trajectory.description: Won the Theatre World Award for Outstanding Debut Performance for her role in Once on This Island.

trajectory.title: Film debut in Respect
trajectory.description: Appeared in the Aretha Franklin biopic Respect opposite Jennifer Hudson, making her feature film debut.

trajectory.title: Starred in Power Book III: Raising Kanan
trajectory.description: Was cast as Jukebox in the Starz crime drama Power Book III: Raising Kanan, a major television role.

trajectory.title: Lead role in Cinnamon at Tribeca
trajectory.description: Starred in the lead role of the film Cinnamon, which debuted to rave reviews at the 2023 Tribeca Film Festival.

trajectory.title: Returns to Broadway in Hadestown
trajectory.description: Returned to Broadway to star as Eurydice in the critically acclaimed musical Hadestown, her first Broadway role in eight years.
